clue.text: Illegal drugs attitude embraced by extra footballers?

indicators.note: the stance is held inside the footballers' word, as if hugged by it

parts.note: substitutes, the extra players on the bench, are SUBS
a stance is an attitude or position taken

explanation.surface: Reserve players caught with illegal drugs, a scandal in the dressing room.
explanation.definitionFit: Substances is a common euphemism for illicit narcotics, as in substance abuse.

clue.text: Run off, having caught chap bare

indicators.note: the scrambled letters hold the chap's word inside them, as if catching him
off signals that the letters of the word run go wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or chap

explanation.surface: Someone flees after catching a man without his clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run off' reads as fleeing, but 'off' is the anagram signal, giving UNR; 'having caught' then wraps that around a dated British word for a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: To bare something is to expose or reveal it, a verb synonym.

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A little bird's burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave as an adjective means serious or severe, a synonym for a solemn manner.

clue.text: Stopped and relaxed after a run

indicators.note: after places the relaxed word behind the article and the run

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
to have rested is to have relaxed

explanation.surface: A jogger stopped and took a break once the run was over.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrested means halted or checked, as in arrested development.

clue.text: Architect's arch is unfortunately losing hospital marks

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters of the architect's words have come to grief and are jumbled
losing says one letter is dropped from the pool before it is rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s is counted as a letter here
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An architect's arch, sadly missing its hospital wing, leaves its marks.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ARCHITECTS ARCH IS, with one H removed as 'losing hospital' says, are rearranged as 'unfortunately' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Characteristics are distinguishing features or traits, the marks by which something is known.

parts.note: sh is the hush command telling someone to be quiet
out means completely, as in tired out
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son roars at someone to shut up entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellows as a verb means yells loudly, synonymous with shouts.

indicators.note: over means the word set is turned over and read backwards

explanation.surface: An assessment is arranged after the time runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is an evaluation or assessment of ability or quality.

indicators.note: complicated suggests the letters are tangled up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken strap makes it awkward to carry a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport goods is to carry or convey them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Man flogged? That is start of retribution

parts.note: flogged is British slang for sold
i.e. abbreviates id est, meaning that is

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the following word, retribution

explanation.surface: A man is whipped, and that is the beginning of revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogged' looks like punishment, but in British slang to flog something is to sell it.
explanation.definitionFit: Man as a verb means to staff a post, as a soldier does; or a soldier is an example of a man in the ranks.

clue.text: Measure brill caught in river? On the contrary

indicators.note: caught in would put the fish word inside the river; the reversal of roles comes from the next phrase
on the contrary swaps the roles, so the river goes inside the excellent word instead

parts.note: brill is British slang for brilliant, and so ace
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Checking the size of a brill, a flatfish, landed from a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Brill looks like the fish but means excellent, ACE. 'On the contrary' reverses 'caught in', so R goes inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, an imperial measure of 4,840 square yards.

parts.note: a reason can be a purpose or goal, the end in view
able means skilled or accomplished

explanation.surface: A footballer asks whether the goal was achieved, and gets a curt reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Just in the sense of fair or sensible matches a fair, sensible verdict or price.

indicators.note: right of places the proclaiming word to the right of the abbreviation in an across answer

parts.note: vents means expresses openly, airs or proclaims

explanation.definitionFit: Events are happenings or occurrences, things that are matters of note.

clue.text: Criminal act — is it about rector's description of Constable?

indicators.note: about has the scrambled letters go around the rector's letter
criminal suggests the letters are crooked and rearranged

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: A rector questions whether some offence is criminal, with a police constable involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable looks like a police officer, but it is John Constable, the English landscape painter. 'Criminal' rearranges ACTISIT, and 'about' puts it round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistic describes a painter like John Constable, an English landscape artist.

clue.text: Search for specification on back of packet

parts.note: pro means in favour of, or for
spec is short for specification

indicators.note: back of picks the last letter of the word packet

explanation.surface: Looking for the product details on the reverse of a packet.
explanation.definitionFit: To prospect is to search, especially for gold or minerals.

clue.text: English town is flat in part

indicators.note: in places the flat word inside the part word

parts.note: a stage is a phase or part of a process
even means level or flat

explanation.surface: Part of an English town is flat land.
explanation.walkthrough: Stevenage is a new town in Hertfordshire, north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenage is a town in Hertfordshire, England, an example of an English town.

clue.text: These could make you row as wind initially drops

definitions.text: These could make you row as wind initially drops

indicators.note: could make says the letters of row and as can be reworked into something new
drops says one letter leaves the pool before it is rearranged
initially picks the first letter of the word wind

explanation.surface: When the wind dies away, sailors must take to the oars and row.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ROWAS, drop W (the first letter of 'wind'), and rearrange ROAS. The whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oars are the paddles rowers pull, needed when the wind falls and sails are useless.

indicators.note: leaves says the black letter departs from the dog
